subject: LOD scores and penalties in step-wise approach

messages.author: d18738ddff11a439
messages.subject: LOD scores and penalties in step-wise approach
parts:
Hi Karl, 

I have a query regarding the penalties in the stepwise approach, that I'm struggling to get my head round. In a wheat RIL mapping population, I'm mapping a particular trait. I've run 1000 permutations (using scantwo) and am starting off with a 5% significance penalty, my penalties are: 
      main    heavy    light 
4.292769 6.672851 3.800732 

With these penalties, the penalised LOD model is: a null QTL model. In this case, I then check for QTL with a 10% significance penalty:
 
         main    heavy    light 
3.880631 6.323707 3.813474 

The results return a model with three QTL
Formula: y ~ Q1 + Q2 + Q3 
pLOD:  1.116 

Firstly, using fitQTL with this model, the QTL LOD scores were relatively high (5.7, 4.2, 7.11) so I'm confused how these aren't been detected at the more conservative penalty (particularly if the main penalty at 5% (4.29) has a lower score than 2 QTLs)? 

Secondly, I know the actual penalty used is based on all the penalty factors (main, heavy, light), is there a way to see the actual combined penalty value used? To see how close a QTL or model was to falling below the threshold ect. For instance, what would I include in a QTL results table if I wanted to show the penalties used in the stepwise approach? I've had a quick look at the Manichaikul et al., (2008) paper but can't find an answer.             

Thanks for your time!

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] LOD scores and penalties in step-wise approach
parts:
The LOD scores from fitqtl are comparing the three-QTL model to each of the two-QTL models. It can be that when you have the three QTL, you don't want to drop any of them, but overall they're not better than the null model. Note that the three-QTL model has penalized LOD score 1.116, which is just slightly below 3x the difference between the main effect penalty at alpha=0.05 and alpha=0.10, 3 * (4.29 - 3.88) = 1.23. So with the larger main effect penalty, the three QTL model is viewed as worse then the null model.

It's maybe easiest to focus on models with strictly additive QTL. You can look at the results of scanone(), and then build up to larger models by repeated use of addqtl(). 

You can also run stepwiseqtl() with keeptrace=TRUE, and look through that trace information, which is stored as an attribute of the output and shows the sequence of models and their penalized LOD scores.

karl
